# Stage 3: TypeScript 6.0.3 cycle census

Report only, October 7, 2026. Adamic base `ef3d907ecdc4c771b016f7d9c52372def057a340`; branch `codex/tsc-cycle-census`. TypeScript tag `v6.0.3`, commit `050880ce59e30b356b686bd3144efe24f875ebc8`. No compiler, runtime, upstream source or repository tests changed.

## Decision for the binder and checker

The leading plan is compiler-inferred **checked weak edges**, not a handwritten Weak port. AST parents are the first useful inference case. Debug Type/Signature checker references and the node-builder tracker/context pair are other explicit back edges. Do not infer every checker cache as weak: several caches are the only strong keeper of a newly created target. Flow loops and literal-type self/reciprocal links require more than a parent naming heuristic.

Program keeping a graph reachable is different from Program independently owning every member after its edges become weak. Ordinary CLI no-emit checking keeps its SourceFiles, their ASTs, binder tables and its checker alive through checking. That supports weak links **to those roots and their strongly owned descendants**. It does not establish an independent owner for every synthesized declaration, fresh literal type, instantiated signature, flow label or retired SourceFile. For those, either prove a keeper, add Program-scoped ownership as a separate design, or refuse inference. A loud expired-edge check prevents a silent miscompile; it does not make a prematurely expired cache semantically correct.

**Completeness boundary:** the original compiler cannot yet be lowered far enough to run Adamic's whole-program finder and fresh-write proof. The inventory below exhausts the declared property slots found by the pinned checker in all 77 checked-in `.ts` files under `src/compiler`, including nested interfaces, classes, anonymous type literals, factory and transformer subdirectories. It gives every positive in a separate, conservative type-graph model, plus instantiated container candidates. It is not an observed list of Adamic refusals. Unknown/generic declarations and lexical capture candidates are listed separately; a precise monomorphized/cell census remains blocked on lowering. Counts are of these explicit inventory records, not a claim to have certified every runtime slot or every original tsc write.

## Observations

The doctrine and memory Cycles sections were read before analysis, including the built holder proof across calls. The implementation is in [internal/lower/cycles.go](../internal/lower/cycles.go), [internal/lower/fresh.go](../internal/lower/fresh.go) and `internal/fresh`; native weak handles are in [internal/native/runtime/weak.c](../internal/native/runtime/weak.c). The finder runs **after lowering**, skips type syntax when seeding used types, follows structural views and function-value captures, checks readonly constructor fields as well as mutable fields, and returns the **first** unproven slot. Readonly arrays/maps/sets have no mutable container slots, but their elements/entries remain reachability edges. A Map object key and a Set element cannot currently be spelled weak by the finder; their refusal suggests readonly construction or a fresh-write proof.

The allocation profile was fetched from `origin/codex/tsc-allocation-profile`, [docs/stage3-tsc-profile.md](https://github.com/system-inc/adamic/blob/codex/tsc-allocation-profile/docs/stage3-tsc-profile.md). Its source pin matches this checkout. The original was fetched into scratch with `git clone --depth 1 --branch v6.0.3 https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript.git`. Its checked-in `lib/typescript.js`, version 6.0.3, supplies the checker for this report. No dependency install, generated diagnostics or compiler self-build was needed for declaration inspection. This does not replace the profile's complete self-check setup.

### What ran through Adamic

A scratch `.a` file containing exactly the 523 top-level interface declarations copied from `types.ts` was passed to `go run ./cmd/adamic c interfaces.a`. Exit 1, before lowering: for example `interfaces.a:1001:28: error TS2503: Cannot find namespace 'SyntaxKind'`, and missing `__String`, `JsxChild` and other aliases. Interfaces alone are not a closed input. Inventing placeholders for those types would falsify the graph; they were not invented. `adamic types` only loads/checks types and is not a cycle-finder run. A declaration-only successful emission would also not certify writes absent from that input.

Four small scratch `.a` projections, not copies of the full tsc implementation, exercised the actual finder/proof:

| Input/control | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Node-shaped parent and mutable children; push child, then `child.parent = parent` | Refused `CompilerNode.parent`, naming that write, `adamic/cycle-capable`, exit 1. |
| Label-shaped node made in a literal with `next: previous` | Accepted; sanitizer build and Node both print `1`, exit 0. |
| Mutation control replacing that construction by `label.next = label` | Refused `ActiveLabel.next`, naming the self-write, exit 1; Node accepts and prints `x`. |
| Weak parent, local fresh factory calls and child-array push | Accepted; sanitizer build and Node both print `1`, exit 0. |
| Ownership mutant of that Weak tree: drop the last parent variable while child survives | Sanitizer build succeeds; native prints `adamic: panic: a weak reference was read after what it pointed to was freed`, exit 70. Node prints `1`, exit 0. No sanitizer error is needed to catch it. |

The first Weak-tree attempt used `?.` to read a number and hit a lowering NotYet. Its second attempt at module scope refused the child-array write: global storage had exposed the holder/value. Moving the builder's locals into a named function made the same tree pattern provable. These are recorded failures, not successful proof runs over tsc.

An external pinned-TypeScript virtual-source Program, with `strict`, `noEmit` and zero diagnostics, observes that a declaration's symbol occurs in the SourceFile export table, `symbol.declarations` contains the declaration, and parent/child identity agrees. It also observes a real `regularType.regularType === regularType` self-cycle. The initial probe incorrectly expected the returned literal type to have `freshType === itself`; that assertion failed and is retained in `live-initial.log`. The corrected probe reports `literalSelfFresh: false, literalRegularSelf: true`. Source writes explicitly show additional fresh-type self-links; they are source observations, not that probe's result.

### Separate graph model

`census.cjs` uses the pinned TypeScript checker, walks declarations first, and tests reachability through unions/intersections, declared fields, structural subtype views, readonly/mutable array elements, Map keys/values and Set elements. A relation step `A ~ B` means either direction is assignable, as the real finder's `related` does. It is a possible view of the holder, **not an assertion that a real object has a pointer to an object of class B**. Function-typed edges add lexical captures of assignable arrow/function expressions and object-literal methods; function returns are not treated as owned edges. Global references are not capture cells. Native method/accessor/instantiation lowering can change which function values and cells exist; that part is still a model.

NodeArray is modeled as its readonly element storage, and JSDocArray as mutable element storage plus its cache. Stock-library symbol metadata such as `Symbol.unscopables`, absent from Adamic's prelude, is excluded. Empty structural types are deliberately not excluded: `Diagnostic.reportsUnnecessary?: {}` and structurally empty classes can make an otherwise unrelated holder cycle-capable by type. Those witnesses are retained and flagged as type-view cases. They are not evidence of an observed live diagnostic cycle. Nominalizing this model alone would hide cases the current finder considers.

Direct dotted assignments were collected as **name-based write leads**, with receiver type, location and source text in the scratch JSON. A row's lead is not a complete alias-resolved write census: literals, spreads, getters/setters, `Object.assign`, helper mutations, element stores, append/map helpers and generic views also matter. No lack of a lead is taken as a general freshness proof. Shortest witnesses can use broad structural views or unrelated assignable callback signatures; that conservatism mirrors the finder rather than proving actual runtime membership. All production inventory rows below are **reasoned/model**, never marked as real-finder runs. The projections above are the only new real-finder runs.

## Count and patch size

| Inventory category | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| (a) proposed checked weak backlinks | 80 |
| (b) source-local fresh construction | 2 |
| (c) hard or not yet justified | 1603 |
| Total positive records | 1685 |
| Inferable and right, with stated lifetime contract | 2 |
| Inferable but ambiguous over the whole slot | 774 |
| Not inferable from this type/write evidence | 909 |

There are 3,186 declared property records in 1,121 interface/class/type-literal holders. The model expanded 4,379 types and inspected 1,708 lexical function values. Its positives are 1,535 declared-field records and 150 instantiated container-slot records. Inherited fields are not repeated unless an interface redeclares/refines them. Several anonymous refinements share a physical source line; record counts, logical runtime field counts and changed source lines are different quantities. Container aliases/type identities may describe the same storage schema; they are kept as separate analyzed instantiations rather than allocation counts.

For the proposed (a) subset, a non-mutating property-symbol census found **80 declaration records on 78 existing source lines**, in `types.ts` and `checker.ts`. A mechanical manual spelling patch needs those 78 lines plus two Weak-import lines: **80 annotation/import lines**. It also found **1,203 distinct source lines reading the selected properties**, with 31 lines assigning them. Rewriting every such read to a checked extraction gives a counted dry-run footprint of **1,281 existing lines plus two import lines = 1,283 lines**. Plain target assignments need not change for Weak's brand. This is an explicit all-read rewrite scenario, not a finished typechecking patch: three unresolved named accesses, aliases, inferred object types, generic/readonly refinements and the (c) cases can add work. There is no justified exact whole-compiler Weak-patch total yet. Under inferred checked weakness the intended source patch is **zero tsc lines**; compiler/runtime work is outside this unit.

The 71 top-level unknown/type-parameter fields and 2,591 lexical reference leads are outside that sum. Primitive capture leads are not cycle-capable; uninstantiated generics are not judged by the real finder until instantiated. Their appendices prevent an apparently exact positive count from concealing the remaining lowering work. Neither (c) nor “not inferable” means a real finder run has refused that original field; it means this report cannot justify (a) or all-writes (b), or cannot choose a unique ownership edge from available type/write information.

## Handling and inference columns

Each inventory row names its rule below, in addition to its holder, field and shortest return witness. The rule supplies the proposed handling, fresh-write assessment, keeper, lifetime risk and the three requested signals. `R` = target already strongly owns holder at the write; `O` = written once after that reachability exists; `D` = name/type distinguish one direction. “Partial” is not a whole-slot proof. Inference “right” is a design assessment for that particular direction, not an implemented inference pass. Names are hints; they never prove strong lifetime.

| Rule | Handling and fresh-write assessment | Strong keeper and later reads | R / O / D; inference assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P | (a) checked weak AST `parent`, including refined parent declarations. Binder traversal closes a real cycle; freshness cannot prove that close. | Program's SourceFile array/map owns roots; child fields/readonly NodeArrays own descendants. A child's ownership of its parent is unnecessary while that tree is kept. Detached children, old versions and synthetic parents need an additional keeper or can expire. | R=yes in ordinary `forEachChild` binding, partial globally; O=no, reparent/rebind/helper writes; D=yes. Ambiguous for the entire slot because `setParent` itself does not assert inverse membership and synthesized scopes are exceptions. Same human edge on the ordinary AST subset. |
| SP | (a) checked weak `Symbol.parent`. Not all writes fresh: merged and late-bound symbols can already be exposed. | Enclosing AST symbol/table, module exports/members and Program/checker roots keep the containing symbol. A synthesized parent that lacks those roots must be kept explicitly. Retained symbols after old Program disposal may expire. | R=partial: often parent.members/exports owns child; O=no; D=yes. Ambiguous globally: checker clones also set parent to an original symbol that need not own the clone. Same human direction where keeper exists. |
| CK | (a) checked weak `Type.checker` and `Signature.checker`. Constructor writes on fresh holders can individually be proven, but their checker/cache inverse closes ownership cycles later. | Program retains its checker during checking; only debug/tracing constructors set these fields in the CLI allocator (`utilities.ts:8489`, `8497`). External service TypeObjects are a separate allocator outside declaration scope. Types/signatures kept after Program retirement can read a checker through service/debug methods. | R=partial, insertion generally follows construction; O=no as stated: once per constructor, but before inverse cache ownership; D=yes. Inferable and right as checker/context backlinks, with a Program lifetime contract. “Written after already owned” is not required for this case; requiring it would miss the useful edge. |
| CT | (a) checked weak `SymbolTrackerImpl.context`; keep `context.tracker` strong. Constructor context write is fresh-holder safe by itself; making the backlink weak permits the later owner write. | `withContext` and its caller's active builder context keep the context through callbacks/tracker reads. Do not let a tracker escape that dynamic extent without also owning its context. This is a call-lifetime owner, not necessarily Program. | R=no at constructor write, yes after context.tracker store; O=no as stated: context is set once before inverse ownership; owner tracker is replaced/restored; D=partial. Ambiguous to a last-write heuristic: it would weaken context.tracker, the wrong human edge. |
| F | (b) retain strong literal-built ActiveLabel.next/breakTarget. No post-construction `next`/breakTarget writes to ActiveLabel were found; a fresh literal holder can point to previous labels/flow targets. The next-chain projection ran. | Active label head/call frame owns the chain; each next strongly owns the previous label. No weak expiry issue. Whole-program generic write matching still needs the eventual lowered run. | R=no inverse owner; O=no inverse ownership, literal initialization only; D=next alone does not prove direction. Not a weak-inference candidate; fresh proof is the mechanism. A self-next mutation was really refused. |
| TREE | (c) keep AST child fields, names, expressions, bodies, lists and owning metadata strong. Factory creates a fresh holder before assigning children, a good relaxation candidate; calls through `baseFactory`/allocator, mutable views, update sharing, setters and callbacks prevent certifying every write here. | AST/tree root owns children. Weakening these rather than parent can free a child immediately. Readonly NodeArray elements require no Weak element patch, but the replaceable field holding the NodeArray is separately judged. | R=partial once child's parent is set; O=not proved globally; D=usually child direction. Ambiguous if judged only at the factory write; human keeps children strong and infers parent on the inverse bind. |
| FL | (c) flow graph: keep straight-line predecessor chains/roots strong, identify loop-closing edges separately. createFlowNode's literal is fresh-holder safe, but addAntecedent pushes existing exposed flows, and checker temporarily replaces/restores antecedents. Flow-to-AST node references can be weak if AST has a keeper; loop edges need an independently owned flow-node inventory or a proven rooted spanning structure. | Nodes/endFlowNode/returnFlowNode, binder current-flow/labels and checker flow caches are partial roots. No observed root owns every intermediate label independently once predecessor slots become weak. | R=partial, loops rather than one parent; O=no; D=no unique direction among antecedents, targets and reductions. Ambiguous; an all-antecedents weak policy can lose the only path to an earlier flow node. |
| SELF | (c) fresh/regular types mix self links and reciprocal ownership in the same field schemas. Self reads may be weak while holder is alive, but a slot-wide Weak conversion can lose the only keeper of a distinct fresh counterpart. | Literal intern maps keep canonical types; a regular type's freshType cache may itself be the keeper of its fresh version. Register both variants independently or infer per-write self/back edges, then prove reads. | R=self or reciprocal, not uniform; O=no lazy initialization and sentinels; D=no unique global choice. Ambiguous; “freshly allocated” does not prove `t.regularType = t` safe. |
| CACHE | (c) symbol/type/signature/node links and caches: many writes publish existing, lazily resolved or synthetic objects. Some links should eventually be weak, but all-writes freshness and independent keepers are unproved. A cache may be the only owner. old cache/type/symbol API values can survive Program replacement. | R=partial or multiple owners; O=no, merge, recomputation, restore and lazy fills; D=partial for target/origin, weak for resolvedType/type/mapper. Ambiguous: selecting every resolved cache loses values; selecting both declaration-symbol directions loses detached graphs. |
| CB | (c) function-valued property. Capture type is part of reachability, not just parameters/results. Prefer capture/owner separation or a direct named function where possible; no general fresh proof for callback-created values. | Captured environment, Program, host or active callback frame must be tracked explicitly. Host callbacks and returned closures can survive replacement; weakening the callback can free the only callable value, while weakening a captured owner can expire during later calls. | R=not established; O=not established; D=no. Not inferable from this signature/write lead; inspect concrete closure identities and lifetime after lowering. |
| VIEW | (c) broad structural view witness, often through diagnostic marker `{}` or empty class. Preserve the field unless its writes are proved confined/scalar; changing all these fields to Weak is not an ownership plan. | Real marker values are usually booleans; runtime scalar writes can pass freshness even when types admit objects. Whole-program proof, rather than the broad view witness, must decide. | R/O/D=not established; not inferable. This is a potential type relation, not a discovered live back pointer. |
| G | (c) other object/reference slot, including resolution/watch/program/transform state. Keep strong and prove construction or isolate a backlink and keeper; no automatic Weak choice justified. | Often host, builder or call-frame owned rather than solely Program. Watchers/resources and resolution closures need an explicit lifetime contract. | R/O/D=not established globally; not inferable. Multiple write/ownership regimes or generic instantiations remain. |
| K | (c) mutable container element/key/value. Fresh literals/new containers and fresh inserted values can pass; mutation of exposed shared containers cannot be certified globally here. Keep owning arrays/maps strong; do not weaken a symbol table or intern map just because its value type cycles. Object keys/Set elements currently have no Weak spelling. | Table/list owner must remain strong; weakening values can erase the owner of target nodes/types. Program arrays own SourceFiles; caches own many synthetic values. | R/O/D=not established for a storage schema; not inferable. Container names and concrete set/push sites can refine a particular instance later. |

(a) proposes an ownership direction, including the stated lifetime precondition. It does not certify all watch/service callers. (b) is a source-local reasoned relaxation case with the named projected control, not a full tsc lowering result. (c) is the hard/unproved set and says why; it deliberately contains potentially provable factory/literal fields rather than pretending their IR summaries already ran.

## Important write sites and alternatives

* **Binder parent:** `binder.ts:2755` calls setParent before bindWorker/bindChildren. `utilities.ts:10703-10707` is a generic setter, with no test that parent owns child. `setParentRecursive` uses traversal callback membership, stronger evidence. `binder.ts:1927` binds binary-trampoline nodes, and checker `8300` attaches a fabricated scope; factory `6763` attaches a cloned name to an old parent that need not own that clone. R/O cannot be assumed for every parent write. Type/name still strongly favor parent as the human weak edge.
* **Declarations and symbols:** `binder.ts:638` writes node.symbol **before** `639` appends the node to symbol.declarations. The second write is the close, so the reverse-ownership signal favors weak declaration entries at this site. Both AST and symbol-table roots exist for ordinary bound declarations. But checker `13843-13846` appends late members, `13942-13945` manufactures index declarations, `33928-33929` attaches a synthetic children declaration, and `25893-25894` copies declarations/parent. `Symbol.declarations` and `valueDeclaration` are therefore CACHE/(c) globally: proposals for source-declaration backlinks do not prove synthetic declaration lifetime. `Declaration.symbol`/localSymbol can instead stay strong to own symbols when they lack a table keeper. Inference must distinguish those roles, not weaken both directions uniformly.
* **Symbols' tables and parent:** `declareSymbol` at binder `749`, parent store `881`, and prototype symbol `3639`. Table values are owning symbol roots. Checker `25894`, `33614`, `37987`, `39187` set parent on clones/synthesized symbols. Multiple locations and non-inverse parent targets defeat a written-once membership heuristic, though parent remains a good weak direction if the parent symbol has its own keeper.
* **Node and Symbol links:** checker `2357-2358` keeps ordinary links in numeric arrays; `2932-2940` returns inline transient-symbol.links or allocates into those arrays. Thus NodeLinks is not simply a Node field, and ordinary SymbolLinks is not uniformly a Symbol field either. For ordinary links, a return path can go through a checker closure/cache rather than Node.symbol. Checker `1993-2007` clears and restores resolvedSignature and type during checking. A write-once cache assumption is false. Transient/Mapped/ReverseMapped symbols do have inline links; type-symbol-links cycles are explicit there.
* **Type.symbol and Type aliases:** checker `5527` associates a newly made type with a symbol, but mapped/spread/synthetic symbols have several owners. A type's symbol is a reasonable eventual weak backlink only when AST/table/checker ownership of that particular symbol is demonstrated. The type graph cannot know a newly manufactured symbol is independently rooted.
* **Type and Signature instantiations, target and mapper:** maps intern/cache results, which then point back to targets and mapper source types. Canonical/erased/base/optional signature caches are lazily filled; some cache results are only held there. A target/origin weak choice is plausible, but self sentinels and source-target sharing make an all-field classification insufficient. TypeMapper is a union of six anonymous shapes (types `7081` onward); its function/deferred variants capture types and contexts. The anonymous entries in the inventory cover those fields; parameter/result signatures alone miss their captures.
* **Literal types:** checker `2101-2108`, `13582-13585`, `20279`, `20287-20288` set self and reciprocal regular/fresh links. These are genuine cycles, not just possible graph paths. A literal type may be new and still close a self-cycle. Distinguish the self write from regular.freshType owning a newly created fresh counterpart.
* **Flow loops:** binder `1375` adds existing antecedents; checker `28922-28924`, `28966-28968`, `29101-29103` replaces/restores FlowReduceLabel targets' antecedents. Node.flowNode closes flow-to-AST cycles; loop label antecedents separately close flow-to-flow cycles. Weak Flow*.node can break the first family while leaving the second. Weakening only Node.parent cannot solve either.
* **Builder context/tracker:** checker `6677` stores new SymbolTrackerImpl(context, ...) in context.tracker; constructor `54348` stores context. `8082` replaces tracker and `8138` restores it. The last store closes the cycle but is an owning edge. The same last-write heuristic that gets binder declarations right gets this pair wrong.
* **Original, emit and redirected nodes:** Node.original and EmitNode provenance may keep old nodes not otherwise in the current tree. factory `7420` sets original; transform cleanup can clear emit metadata. SourceFile.redirectInfo has redirectTarget/unredirected ownership and prototype accessors (factory `6100-6116`), not an ordinary parent pair. Preserve provenance/redirect targets strongly unless a separate original-version keeper exists. `--noEmit` skips most transforms, but their types are in src/compiler and cannot be omitted from a type census.
* **Program and host closures:** Program `1880` closes over `files`; its checker-host methods call Program. Checker closes over host, caches and sometimes its own checker object. These root cycles are not visible as only data fields on the interfaces. Program `1871` deliberately clears oldProgram to prevent closure retention. A proposed weak host/capture must not free the only host or callback owner; external callers can keep TypeChecker after disposing Program. Most such cells need a lowered identity census, not a generic function-type guess.

## Lifetimes: CLI, watch and services

For ordinary `tsc --noEmit`, Program keeps the current SourceFile roots and source lookup maps, and getTypeChecker keeps the checker while diagnostic work runs. Program `1826` sets files; `1880` returns them; no watch/service replacement runs in that ordinary path. Binder AST parents and symbol ancestors whose targets are descendants of those strongly held roots have keepers until their last CLI read. The CLI may release the Program after finishing and before process exit; this is safe only because no further compiler read occurs. “Until exit” means through the last relevant operation, not that every object is a permanent global. The profile's survivor cohorts corroborate persistence across parse/bind/check but are not native weak-lifetime proof.

For **every (a) parent record**, a caller retaining only a child can later run ancestor/source-file traversal after its former tree root lets go. Watch reuse updates parent pointers, but user-returned old nodes and fabricated parents need not be reattached. Retired SourceFiles are not held by the new Program merely because their children/symbols remain externally reachable. Checked expiration is intentional loud behavior, not source compatibility with V8 retention. For **Symbol.parent**, symbol qualification/accessibility can read enclosing symbols after the former Program/table root has gone. For **Type/Signature.checker**, debug/service accessors can use the old checker while a returned type/signature survives. For **tracker.context**, escaping the builder call can invalidate its local context even while Program is alive. The lifetime column's risks apply to each row carrying P/SP/CK/CT; no row has a universal watch-safe certificate.

Concrete release sites were inspected: `services/services.ts:1888` and `1950` release old SourceFiles in the document registry; `2035-2041` cleanupSemanticCache releases files and sets program undefined; dispose `2044-2046` clears host. `services/documentRegistry.ts:372` begins releaseDocumentWithKey. Watch/service callers may retain diagnostics, nodes, symbols, types or the old Program, so the keeper is the **particular version's** Program/registry/client root, not the latest Program. Keeping an old Program strongly suffices for its owned graph; keeping an isolated child/type does not establish that keeper. No watch or service session was run; these are code-path observations and lifetime inferences.

Inferred checked-weak reads need to distinguish an originally absent optional pointer from a formerly present target that expired. Today `adamic_weak_target` returns null for both and `adamic_weak_target_present` panics on null. Existing explicit Weak can return undefined when guarded/optional. The new plan's “every expired read stops loudly” therefore cannot silently reuse ordinary optional Weak reads; it must check handle/target state even for optional-chain, equality and truthiness reads, preserve legitimate original absence, and keep the upgraded strong value alive through its use. Tests for that inference contract have not been implemented in this report-only unit.

## Declaration inventory

All rows are reasoned/model. D identifiers distinguish anonymous/refined declarations even where source lines repeat. `view` and `~` have the structural meanings above. A write lead is a representative dotted assignment with a matching field name and a receiver mentioning the holder when available; it is not a complete proven write set. Full lead text and receiver types are in the scratch JSON. Rule codes supply each row's freshness, keeper/lifetime and R/O/D assessment. Sources are pinned upstream links, not Adamic .a additions.

## Instantiated mutable container inventory

These are storage slots, in addition to the field which keeps the container itself. Readonly NodeArray/ReadonlyArray/ReadonlyMap/ReadonlySet do not appear as mutable container slots. Rows retain their checker instantiation/alias identity, so identical printed schemas can appear twice. For each, rule K means fresh writes are possible but unproved globally, keeper is the strong owning list/table, and no unique weak inference is justified from the schema alone. Object Map keys and Set elements need a different representation or proof, not `Weak<T>` as a key.

## Lexical capture boundary

The source walk found 2,591 distinct outer lexical-reference declarations used by 1,708 arrow/function-expression/object-literal-method values. It includes primitive variables and references to named functions, which need not become owning capture cells after lowering. These are **not 2,591 proven cycles**, and are not added to the positive count. In particular a number/string/boolean cell cannot reach its holder; direct named-function references can be lifted without a closure object. A precise count requires the lowered Environment/Local.Captured identity graph, which the original compiler did not reach.

For the core unit, the object/function-valued leads below remain (c) pending cell identity: an owner captured by a callback can reach that callback through a field/container, and a callback-valued cell can hold itself. R/O/D cannot choose a unique weak cell without the keeper and escaping-call analysis. Additional reference candidates outside binder/checker/program are retained in `census.json` in the evidence bundle; transformer and host callbacks do not disappear from the field/container model above.

## Validation and reproducible evidence

Scratch tooling, inputs, source manifest, JSON, logs and the pinned source are under `/workspace/scratch/tsc-cycles`; `tsc-cycle-census-evidence.tar.gz` contains the small tooling/JSON/log evidence without the upstream checkout. No scratch script is added to Adamic source, and all new Adamic probe files use `.a`.

Commands were run with output redirected to logs, never piped:

```sh
bash cloud/setup.sh > /tmp/tsc-cycle-setup.log 2>&1
source /workspace/adamic-tools/env.sh
node SCRATCH/census.cjs > SCRATCH/census.log 2>&1
node SCRATCH/patch-count.cjs > SCRATCH/patch-count.log 2>&1
node SCRATCH/live.cjs > SCRATCH/live.log 2>&1
go run ./cmd/adamic c SCRATCH/interfaces.a > SCRATCH/interfaces-adamic.log 2>&1
go run ./cmd/adamic c SCRATCH/parent-cycle.a > SCRATCH/parent-cycle-adamic.log 2>&1
go run ./cmd/adamic c SCRATCH/self-label.a > SCRATCH/self-label-adamic.log 2>&1
go run ./cmd/adamic build SCRATCH/weak-parent.a -o SCRATCH/weak-parent --sanitize > SCRATCH/weak-parent-build.log 2>&1
go run ./cmd/adamic build SCRATCH/detached-parent.a -o SCRATCH/detached-parent --sanitize > SCRATCH/detached-parent-build.log 2>&1
go run ./cmd/adamic build SCRATCH/fresh-label.a -o SCRATCH/fresh-label --sanitize > SCRATCH/fresh-label-build.log 2>&1
go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/lower ./internal/fresh > SCRATCH/lower-fresh-tests.log 2>&1
go test -count=1 -v -timeout 30m ./internal/oracle -run '^(TestTheOracleCatchesOneByte|TestFreshWriteProbesStayRefused|TestReadonlyFieldsAreJudgedByTheirConstructorsWrites|TestWeak.*)$' > SCRATCH/filtered-oracle.log 2>&1
python3 SCRATCH/validate.py > SCRATCH/validation.log 2>&1
```

`internal/lower` passed in 12.465s, `internal/fresh` in 18.487s; filtered oracle passed in 7.537s. The oracle includes the existing deliberate one-byte output mutation, refused fresh-write probes and explicit weak expiry behavior. The regex also named TestReadonlyFieldsAreJudgedByTheirConstructorsWrites, which is not in the oracle package; readonly probes were exercised by the existing suites, not by a newly invented test of that name. This report changes no package code; the full uncached repository gate was not run.

| Mutation/control actually run | What caught it |
| --- | --- |
| Label literal builder replaced by self-next assignment | Actual Adamic cycle-capable refusal names the self-write. |
| Weak tree's last strong parent owner dropped before read | Actual native checked-present weak read panics with exit 70; external Node prints 1. |
| Existing one-byte native output mutant | TestTheOracleCatchesOneByte passes, demonstrating rejection by Node byte comparison. |
| Inventory Node.parent row deleted | Independent required-root inventory assertion fails in validate.py. |
| A listed source field renamed to a nonexistent field | Validation of field spelling against pinned source fails. |
| Count of (a) increased without a record | Independently recomputed counts fail. |
| Literal self-cycle classified as fresh/relaxed | Known-source-self-cycle assertion fails; external live Program independently observes regularType self-cycle. |

Validation mutants change in-memory copies of report data, never the compiler/runtime. They establish that the report's sanity checks fail for their intended corruption. They do not validate the whole graph model against native lowered tsc. The first closure-expanded graph run was stopped for excessive repeated type formatting; the final run caches labels and finishes. Failed interface/Weak lowering/initial live-probe logs are retained rather than hidden.

Not covered: original tsc lowered to Adamic IR; a run-generated complete refusal list or complete freshness verdict; arbitrary subtype/object-literal/accessor shapes hidden by unsupported lowering; every concrete generic instantiation; exact owning capture-cell identity and counts; a compiled manual Weak patch; every weak-target keeper; a watch/language-service execution or native tsc CLI run; inferred checked weakness itself; a mutant of that unimplemented inference. The declaration/container positives and the explicit unknown/capture boundaries are the reviewable census available now.

## Inference recommendation and final count

Infer candidates from a concrete inverse strong field/array/Map membership and allocation/write history, then separate **edge selection** from **keeper lifetime**. Requiring writes-once misses merging/rebinding, while choosing only the write that closes a cycle weakens the tracker owner and can weaken owning cache entries. A name/type direction can prioritize a parent/checker backlink; it cannot replace inverse membership and keeper proof. Self links need special handling, and a schema mixing self and owning links needs either per-write representation or separately rooted targets. Retain unresolved owning edges strongly and refuse the residual cycle, rather than silently infer a premature weak cache.

If the CLI strategy is that Program literally owns every allocation until its last read, make that ownership concrete and independently checkable, including synthetic/flow/cache objects. Today's root graph and V8 survivor profile do not establish that stronger claim. Once that owner exists, inferred weak edges can safely cut more SCC edges during the Program's lifetime; watch/service epochs and teardown remain separate contracts. No such registry/region or inferred-edge implementation was added here.

For the 1685 declared/container positive records: **inferable and right 2; inferable but ambiguous 774; not inferable 909**. Handling: **(a) 80, (b) 2, (c) 1603**. The 71 unknown/generic declarations and 2,591 lexical-reference leads remain outside those counts pending concrete lowering.
